findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed that the trash can in the all genders bathroom did not have a lid. PIC was notified. Ensure that all bathrooms that are used by women have a covered trash receptacle for feminine products for hygienic purposes and to protect facility plumbing.
findings.citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
1ST REPEAT: Observed the following areas in a state of disrepair:
(i) The wall above the handwashing sink was observed to have an open seam and rots beneath the wires.
(ii) The ceiling tiles above the prep table, the triple sink, and entrance to the back prep area were crumpled and peeling.
PIC was notified.
Ensure that these areas are sealed by the next routine inspection properly, providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface, and preventing possible contamination if pieces were to fall into food.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.16(B) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The soda nozzles were observed to have to be soiled. PIC was made aware. The soda nozzles were removed to be cleaned. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The trash can in the all genders bathroom was observed without a lid. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that trash cans within bathrooms used by females have a lid to conceal their contents.
findings.citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following were observed,
1. The wall above the handwashing sink was observed to have an open seam and rots beneath the wires. 
2. The ceiling lines above the prep table, the triple sink, and entrance line to the back prep area were observed in disrepair.

PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspectors that the that the necessary repairs will be done. Ensure that these areas are sealed properly providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.16(B) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed employees were not using a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The PIC was informed and they will be educating employees about the proper hand washing procedure. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed employees were removing gloves and donning new gloves to engage in food preparation without hand washing in between. The PIC was informed and they will be educating employees about the proper hand washing frequency. Ensure that employees always wash hands before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with food.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed that the caulking sealing the triple sink to the wall is degrading in quality. Ensure that the caulking is removed and replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there are several holes in the wall directly above and to the left of the hand sink. The holes must be sealed (ex.caulking) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the holes are sealed by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed several holes in the wall above the hand washing sink. The holes must be sealed (i.e., caulked) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Additionally a portion of the ceiling above the hand washing sink is peeling. The ceiling must be reattached to create a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure the holes are sealed and the ceiling is reattached by the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed employees failing to use a barrier to turn off the faucet after handwashing. The employees were educated when the inspector observed the violation. The PIC was also instructed to educate their employees on the proper hand washing procedure. The inspector also suggests getting an automatic paper towel dispenser. The current paper towel dispenser requires employees to use a handle to get paper towels. Having an automatic dispenser would make it easier for employees to get paper towels to turn off the faucet. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing to prevent contamination. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed foods in the open cooler being stored at 47F to 55F (ambient air). A package of cheese had an internal temperature of 51F (probed). The food had only been in the cooler since the morning. The PIC moved the food into different coolers which were holding temperatures below 41F. The food moved included cut deli meats, various cheeses, and containers of RTE meals/snacks (i.e., potato salad, noodles). For information about the cooler, see violation #33.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Observed the open cooler was holding TCS foods above 41F. The food was removed and a reflective sheet was placed over the top of the cooler to help lower its temperature. The PIC stated that they sometimes have issues with the cooler when it is extremely hot, and Springfield is currently in an excessive heat warning. The PIC should not put food back into the cooler until it is consistently holding temperature at 41F or below. The inspector will return on 09/06/2024 to ensure that the cooler is holding TSC foods at 41F or below. For information about the food, see violation #22.

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
At the start of the inspection, there was no CFPM present. One of the two CFPMs arrived at the facility during inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that a CFPM is present at all times to cover all hours of operation. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed an employee rinsing hands in the triple sink. Discussed with PIC to educate staff that handwashing should only occur in handwashing sinks. Ensure that triple sinks are used for ware washing and not handwashing.

6-301.13: A sink used for FOOD preparation or UTENSIL washing, or a service sink or curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water or similar wastes, may not be provided with the handwashing aids and devices required for a HANDWASHING SINK.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S).

The person-in-charge is responsible for ensuring the facility remains in compliance with 2017 FDA Food code requirements. The number of repeat violations and priority/priority foundation violations observed today indicate a need of more effective active managerial control of the facility. A follow-up is issued for 10/05/2023 to check overall compliance and active managerial control of the facility. Ensure that training is properly execute to prevent future violations. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (A) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations not conducted in private home/room with sleeping quarters;  (B) restricted access ; (C) visitors comply with Code; (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;  (F) approved source/unadulterated;  (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ; (I) monitoring temperatures; (J) consumer advisory conveyed; (K) proper sanitizing;  (L) buffets are controlled;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of responsibility to report information about health; (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a staff member wash hand using proper procedure EXCEPT for less than 20 seconds (approximately 5 seconds of active scrubbing). Ensure that all staff are aware of proper proceure for hand washing AND that proper procedure is followed at all times. A follow-up is issued for 09/11/2023. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S).

Hand washing throughout the faciity was poor. Frequency for most employees except management was not sufficient to prevent the contamination of foods being worked with and multiple instances of touching non-sanitized nonfood-contact surfaces were observed. Manager discussed with staff the need to wash hands at all glove changes and at any time gloves may become soiled. Due to the severity of the problem and the fact that this is a repeat violation, inspector will return on 09/11/2023 to evaluate hand washing compliance. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S).

Inspector observed a tray of deli sandwhiches resting on the basin of the hand sink completely blocking access to the hand sink. The tray being present resulted in a manager seeking to wash hands being unable to do so without moving the tray of food. Ensure that hand sinks are stocked and accessible at ALL times of operation. Due to being a repeat violation and the severity of the violation, a follow-up is issued for 09/15/2023.

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several instances of poor food handling resulting in the potential for contamination of ready-to-eat (RTE) foods. The following conditions were observed:
- Foods stored on a hand sink where they must be removed with soiled hands due to the hand sink being blocked.
- Personal phone and keys are observed on a shelf directly above where food preparation was occurring.
- Soiled gloves were used to prepare RTE salads.

Ensure that foods are protected from ALL sources of contamination at ALL times. A follow-up is issued for 09/11/2023.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S).

A wiping cloth is used to soak up grease along the back wall behind the fryers where there is a large amount of grease/oil accumulation on the floor. Wiping cloths may not be used to catch dripping grease and equipment must be functioning properly. Ensure that wiping cloths are not used as grease catches or allowed to sit soiled for any reason.

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S)

Inspector observed the following nonfood-contact surfaces to be soiled during the inspection:
- Large amounts of grease are observed along the sides of fryers and stove in the kitchen.
- Grease dripping from the left side of the ovens is accumulating on the side and floor.
- Food debris is observed on electrical outlets by fryers/hot holding.

This list is not exhaustive. Ensure that all nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned often enough to prevent the accumulation of residue and debris. 

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S)

Accumulations of old food and debris exceeding daily operational accumlations are observed on most hard-to-reach areas of the facility including floors/walls under/behind equipment and the majority of ceiling tile. This has been an ongoing issue of compliance within the facility. Ceiling tile are heavily soiled with grease residue that they are uncleanable at this point in time. Several ceiling tile are peeling due to age and grease accumulation. Under counters and equipment such as fryers and hot holding units are soiled with residue and debris. A thorough deep cleaning is required to bring the facility into compliance. Due to being a repeat violation with no progress made, a follow-up is issued for 09/15/2023.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Several personal items were stored above the back counter where food preparation is occurring. Personal items must be stored in designated areas at all times. Ensure that employees are aware of where to store personal items and that items such as phones and keys may not be stored in food preparation areas. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
The hood system over the hood has been a continual source of dust, dirt and grease residue which has been allowed to accumulate on the ceiling tile of the deli. During the inspection today, inspector observed a visible amount of smoke in the entirety of the building but most prominently throughout the deli area where the fryers and stovetops are actively functioning. Although the hood appears relatively clean with no visible drips developing or buildup of debris, the exhaust is not able to properly disipate materials from the equipment underneath. This poses an imminent public health hazard, nuisance and may constitute unlawful discharge of hazardous materials. Smoke is hazardous to the health of building occupants and may contain other hazardous materials which, when not ventilated properly, will accumulate on items inside the building including food and nonfood-contact surfaces. Lastly, failure to dissipate heat from the equipment below the hood in concert with an accumulation of potentially flammable materials poses a significant fire hazard. Due to the severity of the violation and the imminent health hazard posed by the malfunctioning hood, resolution is required immediately. Per conversation with the general manager, a third-party hood cleaning company is to be secured to investigate the cause of the problem by the end of the day. Failure to have a functioning hood will result in continued enforcement including but not limited to closure of the deli/referral to fire department and/or building and zoning. 

6-501.14: (A) Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. (B) If vented to the outside, ventilation systems may not create a public health HAZARD or nuisance or unLAWful discharge.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Several priority/priority foundation violations were observed. Several repeat violations were observed. Person-in-charge is required to be present during food preparation and is responsible for ensuring that compliance with 2017 FDA Food Code is occurring. This has not occurred during this inspection. As such, an additional follow-up is being issued for 30-days to ensure compliance with Food Code requirements. Work on educating staff on proper procedure. Inspector will return on 05/15/2023.

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
On arrival, inspector observed the hand sink to have a large amount brown, transparent liquid residue and dark brown debris indicating the hand sink had recently been used for dumping or other activity. Hand sink may ONLY be used for handwashing at any time. Hand sinks may NEVER be used as dump or prep sinks. Ensure that hand washing sinks remain accessible and only used for hand washing. During the inspection, the hand sink was cleaned out. Discussed with person-in-charge who discussed with staff. Corrected on site. No follow-up required. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 09/21/2022

On arrival, no sanitizer was available in the facility. During the inspection, sanitizer was made to proper concentration in the triple sink and two buckets of chlorine sanitizer solution were prepared. Sanitizer must be available to clean utensils and food contact surfaces at all times. Enusre that sanitizer is prepared and ready for use at all times and that it is being used frequently to sanitize surfaces in the kitchen. Corrected on site. No follow-up required at this tiem. 

4-702.11: UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The far east display cooler was observed to contain foods at temperatures between 48 and 52 degrees F. Facility provided hanging thermometers indicated a temperature at the vent of 52 degrees F while actively blowing. Inspector had facility immediately cease serving foods from this cooler and discard foods. No logs are kept to determine if foods had been in the cooler for less than 4 hours and could still be used. Foods stored in the walk-in are mixed with remaining food in containers in the display cooler negating the possibility of using foods which have been in the cooler for less than 4 hours. Foods were immediately discarded by staff. The cooler MAY NOT BE USED WITHOUT SCDPH APPROVAL. Facility has been provided with inspector contact information if the cooler is repaired and operating properly before Monday 4/17/2023. If repairs are not made prior to this time, inspector is issuing a follow-up for 4/17/2023 and will evaluate the condition of the cooler and its ability to maintain temperatures under 41 degrees F at all times.  

Facility is also in violation of cold holding temperature requirements by allowing butter to sit on the counter for several hours resulting in a room temperature product which cannot be used. The butter was immediately discarded. Work with staff on maintaining and checking temperatures often and ensuring that foods requiring refrigeration do not remain sitting at room temperature. Consider logging temperatures to prevent such conditions from developing in the future. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
A soiled glove was observed sitting inside-out on the prep counter in the main area of the deli next to the slicer. Soiled gloves are sources of contamination and must be immediately discarded. Ensure that staff is aware of how to handle used/soiled gloves. The glove was immediately diposed of. Corrected on site. 

3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM INSPECTION DATED 9/21/2022

Inspector observed x2 wet wiping cloths on counters in the deli. Wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution at all times. However, no sanitizer solution was available at the start of the inspection for these to be placed in. Sanitizer should have been made promptly to allow operators to place wiping cloths in the sanitizer buckets between active uses. Work with staff on placing wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution of proper concentration or directly into laundry (if heavily soiled/at end of day). 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
PHYSICAL FACILITY CLEANLINESS REMAINS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 09/21/2022.

The air vent in the main area of the deli is observed to have black dust spreading across the ceiling from the vent across adjacent ceiling tile. Clean the tiles and the vent itself and ensure that the vent is cleaned often enough to preclude the accumulation of dust and debris. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
During the inspection of the deli, inspector incidentally observed that there appeared to be a large amount of debris to the left of the fryers behind the display coolers. This is the same area that had many rags soaking up oil and grease from the fryers. Upon closer inspection, inspector observed many mouse droppings in a pile immediately next to the tile for the deli to the left of the fryers behind the upright display coolers of the main facility. The mouse droppings were too numerous to count. The droppings were also accompanied by a significant amount of bedding material. Further down the wall, inspector observed a pile of mouse droppings and bedding material which appeared to be coming out from the wall, possibly serving as an entry for mice. Inspector immediately informed PIC of the droppings and the need to have them cleaned prior to inspector’s return to the facility. PIC was also informed to contact pest control to get a handle on the situation. American Pest Service handles their pest control. Ensure that pests are removed from the facility, harborage conditions are rectified, and that entry into the facility is stopped. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed many wiping cloths throughout the facility. There was a wiping cloth on the floor directly in front of the fryers. Wiping cloths were observed to be packed between fryers. There were many wiping cloths behind the fryers and many wiping cloths packed along the far right side of the hood. Wiping cloths were also observed to be sitting in containers underneath shelving. The only cloth which appeared to be fresh based on the amount/color of soil was the one in front of the fryer. The wiping cloths packed into the hood were soiled to the point of dripping from the hood. Remove these cloths and have them cleaned. If cloths are necessary to preclude the accumulation of grease/oil, remove them once they become soiled and launder them. If cloths are wet, they must be stored in sanitizer solution. Ensure that wiping cloths are used appropriately throughout the facility. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
No sanitizer buckets were prepared during inspection of the facility. Three green buckets were prepared but they were filled with soapy water. No bleach or other sanitizer was added to these buckets when they were placed in service. Inspector discussed with PIC and another manager that sanitizer must be available and at proper concentration during ALL operational activities of the facility including but not limited to cleaning and food preparation. PIC explained that they had been dumped following the lunch rush. Ensure that when sanitizer buckets are dumped, if the facility is still in operation, they must IMMEDIATELY be refilled with water and sanitizer to the required concentration. This is a repeat violation from the previous inspection performed on 02/07/2022. 

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The wire racks sitting directly to the west of the door to the walk-in cooler/meat area of the facility are observed to have a significant amount of residue and dust accumulating on the shelves. Clean utensils and containers sit inverted on this surface. Remove all utensils and containers and clean them and then ensure that the wire racks (both the black and red one) are cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that all surfaces which will be contacting the food-contact surface of containers and/or utensils are kept clean.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the triple sink and hand sink had caulking which had begun to mold and/or deteriorate. The hand sink and triple sink must be re-caulked to create a surface which is smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Ensure that these sinks are re-caulked by the next routine inspection.

There is a ceiling tile which has begun to fall over the hot holding display cases. This ceiling tile must be replaced. Replace with a ceiling tile that is smooth and easily cleanable. Keep an eye on other ceiling tiles which are begin to become soiled and sag from the ceiling that if they become damaged or operators are unable to keep them clean, that they are replaced. 

6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the area underneath the dish machine has built up a large amount of residue and debris and also subject to continuous moisture from the dish machine dripping. The dish machine must be pulled out and the floor underneath it must be cleaned. Ensure that equipment within the facility is moved routinely to clean underneath if there is not clearance to clean it in place.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: Observed the deli hand sink to have a soap and water bucket sitting inside it at the start of the inspection. Ensure the hand sink is used only for hand washing and nothing is placed inside the hand sink. The bucket was moved during the inspection to correct the violation. 
(A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: Observed no maximum registering thermometer or temperature test strips available for the dish machine. Also, there were no chlorine test strips available during the inspection. Temperature test strips and chlorine test strips were provided during the inspection. Test strips were also ordered. Ensure test strips are provided. 
A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: Observed only a bucket of soap and water being used to wipe counters and surfaces off. Ensure a sani bucket is used with an approved sanitizer to sanitize food contact surfaces and equipment. A sani bucket was prepared during the inspection. 
(A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: 2-301.14: Observed deli employee handle a bottle of water and a cell phone with gloved hands. Employee then handled food without changing gloves or washing hands.  Hands must be washed before a new pair of gloves are put on. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: 4-904.11: Observed the metal strips in the knife rack in the kitchen to be rusted. Replace knife rack. (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment: 6-202.11: Observed 4 light fixtures on ceiling in deli to have exposed light bulbs that are not shielded. Provided shields for all light bulbs in food prep areas. Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated or otherwise shatter-resistant in certain areas.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: 2-301.12: (A) Observed two deli employees wash hands and not use a barrier to turn off faucet.  Use barrier to turn off faucet after hand washing to avoid recontamination. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-602.11: (D) Observed blade of counter mounted can opener in deli kitchen to be heavily soiled with food debris.  Wash, rinse and sanitize can opener blade.FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: 6-501.16: Observed mop with wet head to be stored in mop bucket.   After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: Observed Equipment not properly Air-Dried after cleaning and sanitizing at 3-compartment sink. After cleaning and sanitizing all equipment and utensils shall be air dried before use. Corrected. Education provided. Equipment will be properly cleaned and stored. Reference 4-901.11.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
All CFMs must have certified allergen training. Ensure all CFMs are certified. Obtain certificate. 
PA 100-0367. All certified food protection managers (CFPMs) working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed corn on steam table to be at 117F (probed). All hot held products must be maintained at 135 or higher. Corrected. Corn will be reheated rapidly to 165.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) corn at 117 (p)°F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly reheated to above 165°F. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).
